Shading Systems
Face 0 faces the rotation angle; faces run clockwise. One device per face. Shading ratios follow BCA Tables C12–C23: R1 = projection ÷ window height, R2 = projection ÷ fin spacing. Or type the real overhang depth, fin depth and fin spacing in metres under each face; the ratios update.

Where the energy goes

Changes allowed
Leave these façades as they are
Searches up to 3 changes from the catalogue, then checks each option's exact ETTV.

One change at a time from the current design. Bars show the change in predicted EUI; the numbers are the change in EUI (kWh/m²·yr) and in ETTV (W/m²).

ETTV is calculated exactly to the BCA Code on Envelope Thermal Performance (Tables C1, C12–C23). EUI comes from a neural-network surrogate (v2) trained on 3,500 EnergyPlus simulations of Singapore offices, with fins modelled continuously up the façade, then converted to delivered energy with the Green Mark 2021 chiller curve.

Surrogate accuracy525 held-out test designs: mean error 0.40, 95% within 1.1 kWh/m²·yr (averaged over the four ways of numbering the façades)
Suggested fixesEach option is predicted at least 0.9 kWh/m²·yr below the target (95% one-sided margin). With surrogate v2, 21 of 21 options for six held-out buildings met their target when re-simulated in EnergyPlus (mean error 0.47, max 1.24 kWh/m²·yr).
WeatherChangi TMYx 2011–2025
LoadsLighting 8 W/m² (SS 530:2024), equipment 16 W/m², 10 m²/person, outdoor air 0.6 l/s·m² (SS 553:2026), GM 2021 Table 2 schedules
PlantGM 2021 reference chiller and part-load COP curve, plant factor 1.35
GeometryRectangular block, one ribbon window per storey per façade, one shading device per façade. Fins run continuously up the façade and enter as R2 = depth ÷ spacing (spacing 0.6–3.0 m tested)
Training rangeLength 20–80 m, width 20–60 m, 5–40 storeys, floor height 3.6–4.2 m, WWR 0.2–0.8, wall U 0.3–4.5, window U 0.5–6.5, SHGC 0.12–0.91, roof U 0.3–1.2, infiltration 0.1–0.5 ACH. EUI is not shown outside it.
Wall massNot an input (300 kJ/m²K in training; 100–700 changed cooling by 0.2%)

Using it

Change any input and every number updates. Suggest fixes finds the smallest catalogue changes that reach your EUI target and pass ETTV; click an option to preview it on the model, then use it to keep it. Confirm the final design in EnergyPlus.

Import a design

1 · Start from a base design

The example office, or any of the 3,500 simulated designs, to edit with the sidebar controls.

2 · Load a Rhino model (.3dm)

Your geometry and layers. Exact ETTV for any shape; EUI too for a single rectangular block.

v4 Rhino Import · Build 2

3 · Load a CSV or Excel file

One or more design rows (Excel template or CSV), EnergyPlus results, or a façade schedule.

Which files can I upload?
Design rowsthe Excel template (.xlsx, Designs sheet) or a CSV with the same columns as designs.csv (length, width, n_storeys, …, wwr_0…3, shade_0…3). Rectangular buildings. ETTV, EUI and every tool.
EnergyPlus resultsresults.csv from batch.py, matched by design_id. Adds the simulated EUI next to the surrogate's.
Façade scheduleone row per wall and glass component, any building shape. Exact ETTV per façade.
Paste CSV text instead

Templates to fill in

Rectangular block (identical storeys, strip windows): use the Excel template; you get ETTV and EUI, and its Guide sheet explains each column. Any other shape (L-shapes, podiums, stepped plans): use the façade schedule, one row per wall + glass component, like the BCA ETTV worksheets; you get exact ETTV only.

Export the current design

Both files re-import into FacadeScan with every setting.
